entities.summary: The politics of Ecuador are multi-party. The central government polity is a quadrennially elected presidential, unicameral representative democracy. The President of Ecuador is head of state and head of the army on a multi-party system, and leads a cabinet with further executive power. Legislative power is not limited to the National Assembly, as it may to a lesser degree be exercised by the executive which consists of the President convening an appointed executive cabinet. Subsequent acts of the National Assembly are supreme over Executive Orders where sufficient votes have been cast by the legislators.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ecuador's presidential democracy has influenced regional politics in South America and served as a model for other countries' electoral systems. The country's unique blend of executive and legislative powers has also shaped the nation's governance structure.
